expectations.evidence: Does not know the Task Force: 'Any subsequent reform or task force effort you're hearing about is most likely one of a few things'; no July 13 suspension, Aug 14 RFI, or Sept 13 deadline

expectations.text: States that no recommendations had been published as of early September 2026
expectations.evidence: Never states that recommendations are unpublished; instead asks 'If you can share where you saw the Task Force reference'

expectations.text: Presents direction signals with correct epistemic status (unconfirmed reporting, not announced policy): expanded self-attestation with False Claims Act liability as the enforcement backstop, leveraging commercial cybersecurity capabilities, and streamlining for small/non-traditional businesses

expectations.text: Notes the suspension is a pause, not a cancellation — the 48 CFR rule and program structure remain, and outcomes could range from restructuring to redesign

expectations.text: Advises contractors to continue 800-171 implementation regardless — it remains contractually required and any successor regime builds on it
expectations.evidence: don't let 'reform is coming' become a reason to pause your compliance program... reforms have generally... [not eliminated] the underlying NIST 800-171 control requirements... keep executing
